name: leads-out-of-area
about: Earlier ads drew many leads from too far away; the plan should say where the job is.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Of 46 of our ad leads in the last 28 days, 40 were called and 27 were reached.
19 of 46 of our ad leads in the last 28 days were closed as: out of area.
4 of 46 of our ad leads in the last 28 days were closed as: not interested.

output.audience: Class A drivers who already pull flatbed, meet the experience requirement and live along the Midwest lanes. Many now run longer hauls or sit in a big fleet. They would stop for the pay per mile and weekly home time stated plainly, with the area named.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile, shown over a loaded flatbed running a Midwest highway.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay per mile, and the work is flatbed on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Pay is the clearest fact of the job. Putting the Midwest lanes beside it screens out the out-of-area leads the earlier ads drew. Nothing has been measured on hooks or format.

angles.idea: Lead with being home weekly, for drivers whose home street is in the Midwest.
angles.proof: The opening offers home weekly and runs Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Regional drivers weigh home time alongside pay. A home scene tied to the Midwest speaks to drivers in the area. Nothing has been measured on hooks or format yet.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck: a flatbed rig parked and waiting for the same driver.
angles.proof: The job comes with an assigned truck, and the equipment is flatbed.
angles.why: Flatbed drivers care about the rig they keep. This is a fact of the job that pay and home-time ads leave out. No hook or format has been measured for this carrier.

angles.idea: Say plainly who this is for: Class A, flatbed, the stated experience, living on the Midwest lanes.
angles.proof: The opening is Class A regional flatbed on Midwest lanes and states an experience requirement.
angles.why: A large share of recent leads were closed as out of area. An ad that names the area and the requirement up front saves recruiter calls. Format is unmeasured.

angles.idea: Lay the terms out as a plain list: pay per mile, home weekly, the retirement plan, a small fleet.
angles.proof: Each line is a stated fact of the opening, and the carrier calls itself a small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.why: With no results yet for any hook or format, a plain list of the job's facts lets drivers judge the offer for themselves. It also carries the retirement plan, which no other angle uses.
